Early, unsigned build of Silly MIDI Tools: a native macOS app that turns audio into MIDI.

## What's new since 0.6.2

This release is about what goes into the MIDI files you share.

- **No folder paths in MIDI files.** A transcription used to remember its audio by full path, which includes your Mac's account name. It now remembers the audio by file name only. When you open your working folder, the app removes the path from files saved by earlier versions and changes nothing else in them.
- **Pitch bends are optional.** Basic Pitch writes pitch bends, which can make notes wobble in a synth set to a bend range wider than ±2 semitones. Files you drag out no longer have them, and the export sheet has a switch to include them.
- **Only the notes you can see.** Dragged and exported files leave out notes outside C1 to B6, the range the editor shows. The key in the file name comes from the same notes.
- **About window.** It now says Silly MIDI Tools is made by Sillybit and links to the renamed repository. Finder's Get Info shows © 2026 Sillybit.

## Known limits

- Release builds are Apple silicon only, and are not notarized.
- These changes were checked with the automated tests in a Debug build on an Intel Mac. The arm64 app itself has not been run by hand. Please report anything that looks wrong.
